speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help you, please describe your symptoms in detail and tell me how long these episodes last.

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To better assess this, are you experiencing any tinnitus (ringing in the ears) or hearing loss in the affected ear during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The classic presentation of position-dependent vertigo, especially in a 70-year-old patient, strongly points to BPPV. To confirm this, do you have any history of recent head trauma or ear infections? If yes, we should perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver immediately to visualize the characteristic nystagmus.
